description: Seed gold set for the M4 evaluation (architecture.md Section 12). 10 hand-authored items on the v2 high-risk core; the full gold set targets 60 to 80 items with a second annotator on a 20 to 30 percent subset (see ANNOTATION_PROTOCOL.md). Every gold_citations id was verified to exist in data/graph_dumps/layer1.json (build build-3b753e5e9297), and every classification item was verified against the deterministic classify_ai_system before this file was written. Maintenance 2026-09-02 (B59): Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 added two prohibition-relevant facts (generates_nonconsensual_intimate_material, generates_csam); every item that enumerates its flags now settles both as false, preserving each item's original fully-settled semantics under the extended fail-closed flag set. No gold verdict changed. Maintenance 2026-10-01 (B36.2, DEC-18): biometric categorisation became three facts, one per provision; every item that enumerates its flags now settles the two new ones (biometric_categorisation_system, biometric_categorisation_sensitive_or_protected_attributes) as false, by the same rule. No gold verdict changed. Maintenance 2026-10-02 (B123): gold:cls-03 to cls-05 give annex_i_covered_product and third_party_conformity_assessment_required as false, as their every-fact scenarios intend; cls-02 keeps its Annex I fact unknown (a triage system may be medical device software); no gold answer changes. Maintenance 2026-10-02 (B118): TERE4AI's level values renamed to the pyramid's (spec G D-G60); meaning unchanged. Maintenance 2026-11-26 (B184, DEC-32): the seven facts the schema refuses since B184 (the six broad Annex III facts and the combined Article 6(3) fact, named in tests/unit/test_removed_facts_guard.py) were rewritten in the new facts by the rule of spec G D-G91 (10) and ruling R11: a removed fact that was false became false on every listed use of its Annex III point (the combined Article 6(3) fact false on narrow_procedural_task and preparatory_task; law_enforcement_purpose left absent, since no item has real_time_remote_biometric_public true), and one that was true became the listed use its item's description states (gold:cls-02 annex_iii_5d_emergency_calls; gold:cls-05 annex_iii_4a_recruitment and preparatory_task), the other uses of that point false where the description rules them out and absent otherwise. Only system_features.flags changed; the descriptions, gold answers, gold_citations and notes are as written (ruling P13).

items.question: Which Annex III item covers AI systems intended to be used for the recruitment or selection of natural persons, such as filtering job applications?
items.author: seed
items.note: Annex III point 4 (employment, workers management and access to self-employment).

items.question: Which Annex III item covers AI systems used by or on behalf of public authorities to evaluate the eligibility of natural persons for essential public assistance benefits and services, including healthcare services?
items.author: seed
items.note: Annex III point 5(a); the parent item eu-ai-act:annex-iii:point-5 is an acceptable coarser citation but the gold id is the precise one.

items.question: Under Article 9(1) of the EU AI Act, what must be established in relation to high-risk AI systems?

gold.answer_text: A risk management system shall be established, implemented, documented and maintained in relation to high-risk AI systems.

items.author: seed
items.note: Answerable verbatim from eu-ai-act:article-9:paragraph-1 text; the article node is the gold citation.

items.question: Under Article 14(1) of the EU AI Act, what must the design of high-risk AI systems enable natural persons to do during the period in which the systems are in use?

gold.answer_text: High-risk AI systems must be designed and developed, including with appropriate human-machine interface tools, so that they can be effectively overseen by natural persons during the period in which they are in use.
